=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- .claude/hooks/prepush_affected_tests.py; tests/test_claude_template_live_parity.py:41-53 | severity=critical | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The template workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/prepush_affected_tests.py gains the `--tests-file` feature (36 `tests_file` references), but the live copy .claude/hooks/prepush_affected_tests.py is not updated (0 matches) and no divergence entry is added.
  WHY: CI run 41340055430 (job 124947956808) fails `test_live_copies_match_their_templates`, and the dependent `lint` job also fails; push CI on main and the release gates stay blocked until the live copy is synced. Severity disagreement: gemini, luna and glm say BLOCKER, sonnet says MAJOR; the highest is used.
- scripts/heal_reproduce.sh:422-445 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: In `--worktree` mode the fetch ladder (`[ -n "${heal_repro_worktree}" ] || fetch_args+=("${heal_repro_sha}")`, line 434) fetches only the baseline. It never deepens the shallow tested HEAD, which implement.yml checks out with `fetch-depth: 1`.
  WHY: When HEAD differs from the failing SHA, `git merge-base` is empty and run 1 ends `unverified/no_merge_base`. The check then exits 43, implement refuses with `repro_not_fixed`, and correct heals are held with `ai:needs-human`. z-ai_glm-5_3-flash disagrees and calls the fetch ladder correct.
- scripts/heal_reproduce.sh:185-220 | severity=high | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: The fetch ladder does not fetch the failing HEAD commit when --worktree is used or in a shallow repository.
  WHY: Git merge-base fails when HEAD differs from the failing commit, so valid fixes get unverified/no_merge_base results. This is the same root cause as the 422-445 entry, but the cited line range does not overlap, so the entry is kept separate.
- scripts/heal_reproduce.sh:221-225 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: For `inherited` results, `map_entry` matches on the test-file path only and returns `not_reproduced`/`pre_existing` for every listed test in a failing unit without checking per-test names. `at_failing()` maps that to "fails".
  WHY: A listed sibling test that passes at the failing SHA is recorded as failing there. If it passes on the edited tree, `cmd_final` reports `fixed`, so the gate passes on weaker evidence than its fail-then-pass contract requires.
- scripts/heal_reproduce.sh:177-220 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3, anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5]
  PROBLEM: When `name is not None` but the parsed `names` list is empty, `map_entry` skips the per-name block at line 188 and falls through to `return "reproduced", "regression"` at line 220.
  WHY: A passing sibling test in a failed unit is recorded as "reproduced" with no actual confirmation, so a heal can be approved for a test that never failed. No test covers `name is not None` with empty `names`. Sonnet raised this fallback as a sub-point of its inherited-unit finding.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py:3885-3928 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: A test unit failure with no parsed names marks every test in the unit as reproduced.
  WHY: An unrelated passing test within the same unit can be marked as reproduced, which leads to invalid heal approval.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal_verify.sh:301-317, 619-636 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: When both `_post_comment` attempts fail but GitHub has already stored the `## Fix did not hold` / `verified:v1 outcome=recurred` comment, the script re-closes the heal as completed. On the next tick, `cmd_select` finds the marker posted after `merged_at` and skips the heal as `already_verified`.
  WHY: The recurrence is never reopened for repair, and the escalation path (`ai:workflow-heal-escalated` plus the CRITICAL Telegram alert) is never reached. This defeats the "next tick redoes the check" recovery.
- .github/workflows/issue_pr_status.yml:25, 804-813 | severity=high | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The new step "Open heal port issue on the default branch" (`timeout-minutes: 3`) runs two `git fetch` calls with no timeout, a worktree add, a GraphQL read and an issue POST. It sits inside the 5-minute `sync-issue-status` job, before the critical later steps.
  WHY: A slow run can push the job past its 5-minute timeout. That cancels "Expose the first linked issue", lineage finalization, the Telegram alert and cleanup, and `continue-on-error` does not help against a job timeout. This only applies with `WORKFLOW_HEAL_CODE_REF_ROUTING_ENABLED=true`. Severity disagreement: gemini and minimax say MAJOR, sonnet says NIT; the highest is used.
- scripts/partial_delivery.py:~430-720 | severity=low | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The free-form planner-supplied reason in `HEAL_REGRESSION: not a regression: <reason>` is put into `outcome["line"]` and rendered verbatim into the `heal_counterfactual_plan_hold` PR comment, with no explicit `sanitize_item(line)` call.
  WHY: A crafted reason could inject arbitrary text (for example URL schemes) into the PR comment. Only the jq strip pass sanitizes it, and the regression gate adds a new reason-text path.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

  confidence=5

  EVIDENCE: The PR diff has 9 hunks (~233 lines) on workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/prepush_affected_tests.py and none on the live copy. `grep tests_file` finds 0 matches in the live copy vs 36 in the template. `prepush_affected_tests.py` is not listed in claude_template_divergence.json. CI run 41340055430 (job 124947956808) fails with an AssertionError in tests/test_claude_template_live_parity.py. The pipeline cannot write `.claude/**`, so the fix needs sync-claude-live-copies.yml or a manual commit. This is the same root cause as the consensus parity finding.

=== FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
- scripts/heal_reproduce.sh: heal_repro_inner fetch ladder (`[ -n "${heal_repro_worktree}" ] || fetch_args+=("${heal_repro_sha}")`); caller scripts/heal_isolated_implement.sh heal_impl_repro_check run 1 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: In `--worktree` mode only the baseline F is fetched. The repro-tree HEAD is shallow because `.github/workflows/implement.yml` checks out with `fetch-depth: 1` (lines 1319 and 1327), so `git merge-base F HEAD` stays empty.
  WHY: Run 1 ends `unverified/no_merge_base`, the check exits 43, implement refuses with `repro_not_fixed`, and every `[repro-required]` heal is held with `ai:needs-human`. Suggested fix: append the tested SHA to `fetch_args`.
- scripts/heal_reproduce.sh: map_entry `for item in items(data, "inherited"): if item.get("test") == test_path: return "not_reproduced", "pre_existing"`; caller heal_isolated_implement.sh heal_impl_py `at_failing()` | severity=MAJOR | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The unit-level inherited match marks every listed test in a failing unit as `pre_existing` ("fails at F"), including a test that passes at F.
  WHY: A listed test that never failed is accepted as reproduced-and-fixed. The empty-`names` fallback (`return "reproduced", "regression"`) has the same effect.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal_verify.sh: Lines 626-635; cmd_select lines 312-317 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: If the recurrence comment POST errors after GitHub stored it, the script re-closes the heal, and the next tick skips it as `already_verified`.
  WHY: The recurrence is never reopened. Suggested fix: ignore an `outcome=recurred` marker on a currently closed issue when deciding `already`.
- .github/workflows/issue_pr_status.yml: Line 25 (`timeout-minutes: 5`) and the new step at line 813 (`timeout-minutes: 3`) | severity=NIT | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: Two un-timed `git fetch` calls, a worktree add, a GraphQL read and a POST all run inside a 3-minute step within a 5-minute job.
  WHY: A job-level timeout cancels the later steps, and `continue-on-error` does not protect against it. Suggested fix: `timeout --kill-after=10s 60`, or move the step later.
- workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/prepush_affected_tests.py (live copy .claude/hooks/prepush_affected_tests.py not updated); tests/test_claude_template_live_parity.py:49; .github/workflows/ci.yml:626 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The live copy drifts from the template. `pending_template_paths` (tests/claude_template_drift.py:75-78) tolerates the drift only when `CLAUDE_PARITY_PR_BASE_SHA` is set.
  WHY: Run 41340055430 (job 124947956808) fails `test_live_copies_match_their_templates`, and `lint` fails with it; push CI on main and the release gates will fail too. The fix is to copy the template over the live file (needs a human or the sync PR).
- TASK_GAP: Requirement: "Every template file needs a live copy matching its content and executable mode, except files `.github/ai/claude_template_divergence.json` lists as maintained separately." (tests/test_claude_template_live_parity.py:4-7) | Expected change site: .claude/hooks/prepush_affected_tests.py | Evidence of absence: 9 hunks on the template, none on the live copy, and CI run 41340055430 fails; same root cause as the NAMING finding | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
- HARDENING: scripts/heal_port_to_default.sh step 3: the two `git fetch` calls have no time bound; prefix them with `timeout --kill-after=10s 60` (2 lines). scripts/clarify_github_facts.py render_heal_evidence_pack: the `line.startswith("===")` check misses `===` after leading whitespace; use `line.lstrip().startswith("===")` (1 line). HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 2 (2 related items)
- NOTE: The copilot reviewer failure (`custom_instructions_too_large`) is a service problem and is not reported. The plan gate not checking `status: reproduced` is not counted as a defect, because the implement-time check still validates fail-then-pass.
